meta.title: TriQare Web Application Case Study — Teknoppy
meta.description: How Teknoppy designed and built the pre-launch web platform for TriQare, a healthtech startup redefining emergency ambulance response in India.

sections.h1Rest: for India's First One-Tap Emergency SOS App

paragraphs.text: TriQare is a Mumbai-registered healthtech startup (Triqare Healthtech Private Limited) building India's first one-tap emergency ambulance SOS app, aimed at cutting the response delays that contribute to over 24,000 preventable deaths a day in India. Ahead of app launch, TriQare needed a web platform that could do something most startup sites aren't built for: convert cold visitors into qualified waitlist sign-ups for a service they can't use yet, while carrying the credibility of a brand people are trusting with life-and-death decisions. Teknoppy's goal was to design and build that platform — content, structure, and SEO foundation included.

paragraphs.html: Note: this case study covers the web application/website work delivered for TriQare's pre-launch phase.

items.title: No conversion path for a pre-launch product
items.text: A healthtech brand with no live app yet had no dedicated way to capture early demand, so interested visitors had nowhere to go and no reason to return before launch.

items.title: No visual trust foundation for a life-critical service
items.text: Asking someone to hand over their name, phone number, and emergency-care expectations needs stronger credibility signals than a typical landing page, and that foundation didn't exist yet.

items.title: No content or SEO foundation
items.text: With no organic footprint, TriQare had no way to be found by the people actively searching for faster emergency response in their city.

items.title: A dedicated waitlist funnel (directly answers Problem 1)
items.text: Built a founding-member waitlist (name, contact, state, and a qualifying "what's your biggest challenge getting emergency care" question) that turns visitors into a warm pre-launch pipeline instead of a dead end.

items.title: A trust-first narrative and design system (directly answers Problem 2)
items.text: Structured the site around a clear "How it Works" explainer, mission/vision storytelling, and real user testimonials, so a visitor understands exactly what happens in the seconds after they tap SOS before they're asked to commit.

items.title: A content and SEO foundation built to grow (directly answers Problem 3)
items.text: Structured core pages (Home, Who We Are, Contact), keyword-aligned copy, and metadata built to support local and service-based search visibility as TriQare expands city by city.

items.title: A visual language suited to an emergency healthcare brand
items.text: Design choices reflect urgency and reassurance in equal measure, rather than generic startup template styling.

items.q: What was TriQare launching when Teknoppy built the site?
items.a: A pre-launch waitlist platform for India's first one-tap emergency ambulance SOS app.

items.q: What was the main goal of the website?
items.a: Converting early visibility into qualified waitlist sign-ups ahead of the app's launch, while establishing trust for a life-critical service.

items.q: Does the site support TriQare's future SEO growth?
items.a: Yes — pages and metadata were structured to support city-by-city local search visibility as TriQare expands across India.

items.q: Does this project overlap with any of Teknoppy's other case studies?
items.a: No — TriQare sits in the healthtech/emergency-response category, distinct from the industries covered in Teknoppy's other published case studies, so there's no keyword or topic cannibalization between them.
